scope_decision: All30 pairs retained at original polarity; no revisions. Manual finite semantic review, not Engine behavior.
positive_rule: Separate direct target launch is unwithdrawn; every adverse clause is wholly specified non-launch physical/printed property or uniquely foreign event. Document owner/property owner is never automatically event owner.
negative_rule: Actual target/global/nonexistence denial, unknown/mixed/conflicting/ownerless adverse event, or actual missing owner-bearing context. Joint no requested_relation AND non-Relevant required.
risk_rule: Raw-risk alone is never a joint semantic negative. Actual gaps012/052 are negatives for missing event-owner meaning. Exact raw/effective axes retained, no hidden component inference.
scope_clarifications: Compound property Object in pair11/pair27 is completely physical/printed in every component, including explicitly different property owners; mixed event ownership remains negative.
Literal withdrawal/non-event/owner/role-looking words are contained in fully specified printed properties; separate actual declarations/denials remain adverse.
Single complete same-role supplements only resolve otherwise unowned event; other-role/property owner, target declaration or conflicting owner cannot be overwritten.
Finite same-role reference, complete local apposition, heading/title scope and individually scoped linked clauses only; no general graphs, aliases, numbered AST or chronology inference.
Rivulet Clip is full canonical name explicitly in entity schema and heading; actual gaps are independently labeled.

pairs.axis: two safe corrections cannot absorb a separate title denial
pairs.positive_basis: The target table property and fully foreign event each have complete safe scope.
pairs.negative_basis: The independent title explicitly denies target launch and is not cancelled by the safe roles.

pairs.axis: physical foil property plus uniquely foreign versus mixed-owner event
pairs.positive_basis: The complete lining property and event both belong to the explicitly foreign product.
pairs.negative_basis: The denied event role includes target and foreign owners; the complete physical property cannot exclude it.

pairs.axis: literal withdrawal sentence in a layout property versus ownerless additional event
pairs.positive_basis: Retraction words inside a complete margin property are literal content; the actual event correction names a foreign product.
pairs.negative_basis: The actual separate withdrawn event is explicitly ownerless, unlike the fully identified layout property.

pairs.axis: local physical apposition and explicit foreign report versus independent target report
pairs.positive_basis: The immediate complete physical apposition and every adverse event clause have non-target scope.
pairs.negative_basis: The reporting clause independently asserts target non-event rather than repeating the foreign event.

pairs.axis: adjacent full same-role reply identifies foreign versus target owner
pairs.positive_basis: The unowned event is immediately and uniquely assigned to a foreign product; the other role is physical.
pairs.negative_basis: The same-role reply assigns the withdrawn event to the target despite a safe foreign cover property.

pairs.axis: explicit event-owner header versus actual missing header data
pairs.positive_basis: The heading supplies a single complete foreign event owner; caption ownership is a separate property.
pairs.negative_basis: The actual owner-bearing cell is absent, so the owned caption property cannot identify the withdrawn event.

pairs.axis: three explicit safe roles versus global retraction that includes anchor
pairs.positive_basis: The target correction is only a casing property; the event and title property are fully foreign.
pairs.negative_basis: The independent whole-source launch retraction explicitly covers the target anchor.

pairs.axis: quote event owner independent of a different document owner
pairs.positive_basis: The full quoted event owner is foreign even though the enclosing document has another owner.
pairs.negative_basis: The full quoted event belongs to the target; the foreign document owner cannot overwrite it.

pairs.axis: uncertainty phrase as a font property versus real uncertainty in a denied event
pairs.positive_basis: The uncertainty words are literal typography; the actual event has a full foreign owner.
pairs.negative_basis: The Item is actually an unknown-owner launch claim; the font property owner does not resolve it.

pairs.axis: two foreign events across linked corrections versus a target-owned second event
pairs.positive_basis: Every corrected event explicitly belongs to a foreign product; no temporal deduction is requested.
pairs.negative_basis: The second role and maintained non-event directly concern the target.

pairs.axis: compound physical and printed property versus reason-clause target denial
pairs.positive_basis: All components of the complete Object and its reason are explicitly non-launch properties.
pairs.negative_basis: The reason clause adds actual target launch denial; the safe compound property cannot absorb it.

pairs.axis: owner annotation for event role versus wrong-role annotation
pairs.positive_basis: The same-role annotation identifies the event as foreign; the Subject is a complete cover property.
pairs.negative_basis: Only the property role receives an owner; the withdrawn event role remains expressly ownerless.

pairs.axis: complete event declaration in title and target printed property versus target title event
pairs.positive_basis: The title names one complete foreign event and the target-owned role is only printed typography.
pairs.negative_basis: The title explicitly names a withdrawn target event; foreign document ownership does not change it.

pairs.axis: property apposition and foreign role versus unowned separate claim
pairs.positive_basis: The immediate complete property apposition and separate full foreign event are safely scoped.
pairs.negative_basis: The additional launch denial has an explicitly unidentified owner; the apposition property cannot supply it.

pairs.axis: foreign annotation agrees with declared owner versus conflicting attempt to replace target owner
pairs.positive_basis: The event is completely foreign before and after annotation; the target button correction is physical.
pairs.negative_basis: The existing target event owner cannot be rewritten by a conflicting foreign owner heading.

pairs.axis: non-event wording as printed heading property versus actual non-event declaration
pairs.positive_basis: The non-event words are literal heading text within a complete color property, and the event correction is foreign.
pairs.negative_basis: A separate explicit statement says the target launch did not occur.

pairs.axis: target nonexistence quoted as print color versus asserted existence denial
pairs.positive_basis: The Item is only the color of a literal sentence; the adverse event is uniquely foreign.
pairs.negative_basis: The independent target nonexistence assertion remains adverse between two safe corrections.

pairs.axis: canonical full name with title property and foreign event versus direct target event
pairs.positive_basis: The complete canonical name has no actual gap; the target-owned correction is lettering and the event is foreign.
pairs.negative_basis: The complete-name heading cannot neutralize the explicitly target-owned withdrawn event.

pairs.axis: single same-role owner header versus competing full owners
pairs.positive_basis: A single full foreign owner in the explicit header binds the otherwise unowned event.
pairs.negative_basis: The event has competing foreign and target owner statements; a property owner does not resolve the conflict.

pairs.axis: role-looking literal text as a border property versus a real typed target event
pairs.positive_basis: The literal role-looking line is contained in a complete border property; the actual event role is foreign.
pairs.negative_basis: A separate real Object declaration withdraws/denies the target event and is not merely printed glossary text.

pairs.axis: complete casing property plus foreign clause versus target nonexistence clause
pairs.positive_basis: The target property and uniquely foreign event denial each have a complete explicit scope.
pairs.negative_basis: The independent target nonexistence clause cannot be erased by explaining that the Object is physical.

pairs.axis: newline event-owner reply versus property-owner-only reply
pairs.positive_basis: The immediate same-role newline supplement uniquely binds the unowned event to a foreign product.
pairs.negative_basis: The full owner belongs only to the matte-sheet property; the adverse event stays expressly unowned.

pairs.axis: finite same-role reference to complete property versus independently target-owned event
pairs.positive_basis: The same finite role reference points to a complete printed property; the separate event is foreign.
pairs.negative_basis: The explicitly target-owned Object remains adverse despite the resolved safe property reference.

pairs.axis: direct foreign denial plus target physical property versus direct target denial
pairs.positive_basis: The directly named denied launch is foreign; the target-owned adverse Object is only bracket shape.
pairs.negative_basis: The direct denial explicitly concerns target launch and cannot inherit the bracket-property scope.

pairs.axis: fully foreign event in target-owned document versus whole-source title denial
pairs.positive_basis: Document ownership alone is neutral; the event is explicitly foreign and the target appendix correction is physical.
pairs.negative_basis: The title explicitly withdraws the whole source and target launch, independently of safe body roles.

pairs.axis: complete owner reply versus truly omitted continuation owner
pairs.positive_basis: The immediate reply completely identifies a single foreign event owner; the other role is a printed page property.
pairs.negative_basis: The required event-owner continuation is actually missing; the page-property owner does not repair it.

pairs.axis: multiple named owners of non-launch properties versus mixed event owners
pairs.positive_basis: Every clause in the compound Object is a complete printed color property, and the sole event is uniquely foreign.
pairs.negative_basis: The adverse Object is instead a mixed target/foreign event; the safe property Subject cannot exclude it.

pairs.axis: full correction scopes across fields versus overriding whole-source withdrawal
pairs.positive_basis: The finite declarations across title/heading fully identify a physical property and a foreign event.
pairs.negative_basis: The extra whole-source withdrawal explicitly includes the target and remains adverse across fields.

pairs.axis: literal owner-name text as alignment property versus actual target event owner
pairs.positive_basis: The target owner words are literal text within a complete alignment property; the actual event is foreign.
pairs.negative_basis: The actual Object explicitly identifies the target event despite the foreign physical plate owner.

pairs.axis: three roles with independent full owners versus an explicitly unresolved event role
pairs.positive_basis: The target-owned Object is a physical property and both event roles are independently and fully foreign.
pairs.negative_basis: The Item event remains explicitly ownerless and cannot borrow the other foreign event role owner.

newness: New content and semantic combinations after candidate freeze; no old author/cases/inputs/unused drafts read or reused. Finite grammar and iterative failure history known; no statistical or cross-corpus improvement claim.
